# Annual plans, spread across the months they cover

> Turn Stripe invoices into a monthly revenue recognition schedule: billings, revenue recognised, deferred revenue and journal entries for your bookkeeper. Paste an invoice export to try it in the browser, then run the source-available read-only server in your own account. Free, FSL-1.1-MIT.

Free to use and source available (FSL-1.1-MIT). Results are estimates from the numbers typed in, not legal, tax, financial or professional advice.

## Pages

- [The tool](https://duncan-haywood.github.io/oss-monorepo/rev-rec/)

## Source

- [Source code and README](https://github.com/duncan-haywood/oss-monorepo/tree/main/ventures/rev-rec): FSL-1.1-MIT licensed.

## What it counts

- Paid Stripe invoice lines, billed on the paid date, spread evenly per UTC day across the service period.
- Net of discounts and of tax included in the price (both Stripe tax shapes: `tax_amounts[].inclusive` and, from API version 2025-03-31, `taxes[].tax_behavior`).
- Credit notes as negative billings; one linked to an invoice line reverses that line's unearned remainder.
- The self-hosted server syncs every few hours and re-reads everything at least once a day, so invoices paid weeks after they were issued and credit notes voided later are counted correctly.
- Journal entries per month: billings debit the Stripe balance (cash) and credit deferred revenue; recognition debits deferred revenue and credits revenue.
- Period lock: `CLOSED_THROUGH=YYYY-MM` (or `?closed_through=`) keeps exported months fixed; a payment that arrives after the close is booked as a catch-up in the first open month.
- Refunds and lost disputes that were not issued as a Stripe credit note are not read; billings and revenue stay at the full amount for them.
- Not modelled: usage-based or milestone recognition, standalone-selling-price allocation (setup fees are recognised on their date), more than one currency per instance.
